title: What the Roof Kept

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The coat keeps a man's shape and the seat keeps his weight; the debt against the tiles keeps his name without ever saying it. Go around all three with a broom, and leave the crack showing.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Vail kiln-house in the kiln month

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and four to two hundred and six days, carried everywhere and told by nobody — six months and twenty-four days to six months and twenty-six days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (a cost asked as a direction answered with the pot and the weather, a carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, likenesses taken down one at a time before they can stand up and call themselves a rule, and an inch of a small hand asked again under a roof the market cannot enter) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no third telling of the shut counting room, no seventh green, no seventh sighting, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Morning the Coat Kept Its Shape
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 204, Ember 25, Fifthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning. No recap of the second-rhythm inch and no boundary drawn at the turning of the tend. The boy is two hundred and four days old and six months and twenty-four days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and four days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings, and overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — three counts in three places that do not become one, because agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that with the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner the house calls the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. One leathery brown-edged crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody will perform. The file is laid out in the small hours as instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth, the held inch on a sixth, the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch. The chapter opens on the household's own keeping of Garl: the salt-stiff coat holding a broader man's shape on its peg, the seat worn hollow by twenty years of his weight, the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned and the new finer grey beside it called the thaw, the proverb gone to the pot, and the debt against a firing of tiles neither paid nor settled nor done with — nobody makes a lesson of any of it, nobody calls a collector and Garl is not collected (T009/T013/T092). Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without a touch, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, feeds him from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve and his mouth unwiped, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without a figure, keeps her finger from beneath the charcoal, and leaves the widow's mark untouched, for a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1 (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, the knife at the very edge of its sill with six checked where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot and Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; he says Yes, house to the early thaw and the late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, chest tight, Ash worked into the knuckle creases, pale clip-ring at the left wrist; the ear-sentence comes to the word that would call the loan and stops with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath is drawn and not spent, nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, and the stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check; no collector comes (T036/T076). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, parting dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeping dusty and clean forearms on one tray; he speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, withholds the full note he knows three turns ahead from a man come up on a wrong wind whose saying about a pot singing early stays a saying with no pot lost, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper of the iron with two bites until Sella's sentence reaches the pot — a remembered holding, not a change made again (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). Three or four unnamed men go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name and no third telling. Asked on the morning, the hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note and comes down at once — the asking is not always answered — and the answer is filed on the sixth place with nothing laid across it (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Seat, the Line, the Uncalled Debt
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 204, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the coat on its peg and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The last tend runs on with no boundary drawn; heat goes off the high air first and stays longest under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one leathery crust keeps its empty place unnamed and no third comes; thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek, temple and wrist, afterdrop waiting. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, uncounted and uncopied, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening (small intake, hold, letting go), pushes the coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, and does not look toward the bed — she never looks toward the bed at the setting (T058/T079, T100). The household keeps Garl by objects and not by a story: the salt coat keeps his shape, the seat keeps his leftward lean, the clean dark line and the finer grey are gone around with a look and a wide step and not swept, the proverb goes to the pot, and the debt against the tiles is circled without a name, worse for being uncalled because it can neither be paid nor settled (T009/T013/T092). Sella's private roll stays unshown, Dessa's cost unentered, and the widow's mark is untouched at a dusk, for a dusk is not an opening. A cost-question brought to the door goes to the pot and the weather and away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after its instruction, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to the ones who want the thaw early and the ones who want it late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot and keeps wanting the late because a late thaw puts off the paying though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went; the ear-sentence comes all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name; he draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it; nine stoppings stand as nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year stands nearer its end than ever and has not given, the Seed 16 breath is unspent and the loan that can hear is uncalled; his stroke goes over the flagstones past the bright patch without the half-check and over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without once turning along it, and no collector comes up or goes down the clay road (T036/T076). Jorra keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel and a pot, withholds his knowing from the wrong wind without making a lesson, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper until the sentence reaches the pot, the iron read again as one piece with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third, He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name is neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number; the arm that has carried him two hundred and four mornings keeps the height of the handle, the give of the shoulder and the turn of the wrist at a step's end, a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost (T009/T013/T092/T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen. In the small hours he lays out the file exact, complete and worth nothing and finds it unchanged; then the hand goes up an inch toward the note through the finger's-width door and holds for the length of the small intake only, coming down before the letting go. It is filed on the sixth place, not a hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, key, power or rule, no payer named and nothing stood up as a sign; he still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift the crust or speak a number.

scenes.title: A Direction From Slate Row
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 205, Ember 26, Sixthday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the yard well and the edge of the clay road. The boy is two hundred and five days old and six months and twenty-five days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred and five days (T088); fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. The chapter's one meaningful change arrives as a direction and not a cause: word comes up from Slate Row, spoken over the boards and not to the basket, that a slate was burned there in the night. Nobody names whose slate, nobody names a man, nobody says which room it came from or why, and the boy files it on a place of its own beside Jorra's grey dust and the two shut-room tellings, without laying it across them and without making it a third telling of the shut counting room; a burned slate is a direction that arrives nowhere and cannot be carried into a chart (T035/T031/T065/T095, advanced and not paid). Jorra comes through from the wheel-shed with the day's meal-fine grey dust ground past the bent finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, goes quieter when the word goes around the boards, speaks to the wheel and a pot and gives the house no name for anything; He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates stays ungiven (T035). The sweet edge of lead glaze comes up off High Kiln on a wrong wind and goes out on the same wind, answered as a direction and entered nowhere, and the saying that a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early stays a saying about a pot and is not made true as a lesson (T064 held). Sella's instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar without a touch, feeds him from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed, keeps her finger from beneath the charcoal, and does not touch the widow's mark, because a morning, a shelf and a word over the boards are not openings and there has been no opening since Ember 1 (T058/T079, T100). At the yard well a rack woman with slip dried pale in the creases of her wrists asks what the pots will want before the kiln month is out and is told to ask the pot and the weather; a man come off the clay road with a number in his fist asks what the kiln will want with the last tend running and is answered with the house and the weather. Both cost-questions go away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). Tarn tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, keeps nine stoppings nine with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T036/T076). Three or four unnamed men go low into the back room before first grey and get no name. Asked in the morning, the hand goes up an inch and holds for the small intake only, coming down before the letting go; filed on its sixth place and laid across nothing (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Word Goes Around the Boards
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 205, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat stays longest in the low places under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one brown-edged crust lies leathery two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist joint, afterdrop waiting. The burned-slate word goes around the yard once more as a direction and arrives nowhere; nobody makes a cause of it, no third telling of the shut room comes, the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack stay entered by nobody, and the boy keeps the new sound on its own place beside the dust and the two tellings with a hand between them (T035/T031/T065/T095). Sella moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger from beneath the charcoal, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, and does not look toward the bed; the widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no other hour (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling the knife lies at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, brings the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, and keeps the stroke over the flagstones without the half-check; nine stay nine, the seventh year presses nearer its end and has not given, the Seed 16 breath is unspent and the loan uncalled; no collector comes up or goes down the clay road (T036/T076). Jorra has gone quieter since the word from Slate Row, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady, tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns ahead and withholds it from the wrong wind with no pot lost and no lesson made, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella's sentence reaches the pot — a remembered holding and not a change made again; the damper stays one iron with two bites joined to no kiln, He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise stays ungiven (T035/T031/T062). At the going of the light Sella carries him home around the pan's gone ring, the bare trough, the rack space, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, and under the roof sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft. In the small hours the hand goes up an inch toward the river's note, stays through the small intake, the hold and the letting go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, and comes down with the breath — the old coordination remembered, not a change made again — and the answer is filed on its sixth place with nothing laid across it (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Last Working Week Runs On
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 206, Ember 27, Seventhday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the coat and the seat, the kindling and the edge of the yard. The kiln month's last working week runs into its third day with no boundary drawn and no shift in the district's two names for the months; the boy is two hundred and six days old and six months and twenty-six days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred and six days (T088); fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that with the sour Ash breath of the corner; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. The household keeps Garl at its closest yet to the end of the tend: the salt coat on its peg, the hollow seat with its twenty-year leftward lean, the clean dark line and the finer grey beside it called the thaw, the proverb gone to the pot and the uncalled debt against the tiles, none swept, none paid, none settled, none made a lesson of and no collector called (T009/T013/T092). Sella gives the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glanced once at the clay jar without a touch, feeds him from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve and his mouth unwiped, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without a figure, keeps her finger from beneath the charcoal, and leaves the widow's mark where it hangs, for a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since Ember 1 (T058/T079, T100). A neighbour at the door with a cost-question about the firing sends it to the pot and the weather with nothing entered (T077). The sweet edge of lead glaze comes up off High Kiln on a wrong wind and goes out on the same wind, answered as a direction and entered nowhere, with no second edge paid and no pot lost (T064). Tarn tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, sets the knife where it can be checked, says Yes, house to the ones who want the thaw early and the ones who want it late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, brings the ear-sentence to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath unspent, nine stoppings nine with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year nearer its end than ever and still ungiven, and the loan uncalled; his stroke goes over the flagstones past the bright patch without the half-check and over the collector's road without turning, and no collector comes (T036/T076). Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust past the bent finger, parts it from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, withholds its note from the wrong wind whose saying stays a saying, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper while Sella's sentence finishes at the pot, a remembered holding, not a change made again (T035/T031/T062). Three or four unnamed men go low into the back room before first grey and get no name; the burned-slate word from the day before stays a direction and not a cause. Asked in the morning, the hand goes up an inch and comes down before the counted breath has finished; filed on the sixth place, worth nothing (T061/T082).

scenes.title: One Rhythm Through the Door
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 206, Ember 27, Seventhday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat stays longest under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one brown-edged crust lies stiff and leathery two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist joint, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody in this house will perform. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting and does not look toward the bed. The widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no other hour; a dusk is not an opening and the last tend is not an opening (T058/T079). The household's keeping of Garl holds to the end in objects: the coat keeps his shape, the seat his weight, the clean dark line and the new finer grey their places unswept, the proverb goes to the pot and the debt against the tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with, and nobody calls a collector (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn keeps the six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip, Garl's unforged sentence beside the knife, brings the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, keeps nine stoppings nine with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year nearer its end than ever and still not given, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled; his stroke goes over the flagstones without the half-check and over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without once turning, and no collector comes (T036/T076). Jorra keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands, tells a pot You'll do, withholds the note from the wrong wind with no pot lost, holds his bent finger in the cold damper until the sentence reaches the pot as a remembered repetition, reads the iron as one bite that holds and one that takes with no Grathic word for both, and keeps He's not Vail sealed and the promise of the name ungiven; the burned-slate word stays on its own place, the two shut-room tellings stay two and no third comes (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road at the half-pace, going wide around the pan's gone round ring, the bare trough, the rack space, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed with a look and a wide step and no number; under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen. In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid with the second reading gone up the road in Berr Clay's locked box and Hessa Rale's slate unread at Greybank, the charcoal unread, the stone cold and unreconciled in its loft pot, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth, nine stoppings nine with no tenth, the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on separate trays with no third gap and no fourth likeness, the carried man's cost entered nowhere, the sixth green still a colour and the foundling still a shape. Then he puts the question to his hand. It goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and, with no breath counted at Sella's fire in the room that does not touch his to hold against, stays up for the length of the river's own low interval and comes down on the next low note — a coordination with the one rhythm that goes through the door, filed on the sixth place as an object of its own: not a longer reach, not a stronger hand, not a hearing (water over water remains a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings), not a seventh, stopping, payment, one of the three held changes, key, power or rule, with no payer named and nothing stood up as a sign (T061/T082 advanced and not paid). He still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift the crust or speak a number. Two hundred and six stands exact in the dark, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody; the fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred and six days, the mark has been touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no other hour, the stone lies cold in its loft pot, the charcoal is unread, the Seed 16 breath is unspent, the loan is uncalled and the seventh year stands nearer its end than ever and has not given. Nothing in the keeping has been joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and the fold takes the hand without a word as the river goes on over water without noticing that an inch rode one of its low notes. The count goes forward into Day 207, Ember 28, Eighthday, and the third and last Account-day of Ember on Day 209.
